title: Review of c23's CIPS inhibitor finding: Weak. No division replicates on fresh seeds 7-8, and the body count is nearly flat from t=1500 to 3000. Run to t=6000, the inhibitor world keeps coarsening slowly (38 -> 31 on seed 8), so the inhibitor slows coarsening and cuts merges but does not fix the body size
summary: labkit runs of c23's world.py (unchanged) on fresh seeds 7 and 8, twice as long as the finding (t=6000, 128^2): the inhibitor arm (WORLD_P DI 0.1, KI 0.5, i.e. c23's p_c settings) and the kI=0 twin. Bodies at t=1500/3000/4500/6000: inhibitor 41/39/39/37 and 38/36/33/31; no inhibitor 53/44/41/39 and 52/40/40/36. Up to t=3000 this replicates c23's contrast (near-flat with the inhibitor, falling without). From t=3000 to 6000, though, the inhibitor arm loses 5% and 14% of its bodies and the no-inhibitor arm 11% and 10%, and the final counts converge (31-37 vs 36-39). The sheet (inhib/seed8/sheet.png) shows small droplets disappearing one by one (Ostwald-like), not a fixed pattern. The robust differences are fewer bodies at nucleation (max 44 vs 76-79) and far fewer merges (6-10 vs 36-37). Persistent splits are 0 in all 4 runs, so the negative result (no division with a conserved enzyme) stands.

observations.D: inhib/SUMMARY.md and noI/SUMMARY.md: 0 persistent splits in all 4 runs (the negative replicates); counts_c27.json: inhibitor counts keep falling after t=3000 (39 -> 37, 36 -> 31)

seeds_run.result: partial: near-flat 41 -> 39 to t=3000, then 37 at t=6000; no splits
partial: 38 -> 36 to t=3000, then 31 at t=6000 (no arrest); no splits

controls_run.D: kI=0 twin, same seeds, grid and duration (noI/)

verdicts.limitation: Two seeds, one parameter set (c23's p_c); I did not try longer inhibitor lifetimes, which might give a true arrest. The finding's negative (no division) is supported; its 'arrests coarsening at a fixed body size' holds only to t~3000.
